h1: Single Tank Deep Fryer with Two Baskets and Mild Steel Stand
short_description: Busy chips joints need a fryer that keeps the oil hot and the baskets moving. This single tank deep fryer has a deep stainless tank with two lift-out baskets, a control knob on the tank and a tall mild steel stand painted bright orange, so it stands at a comfortable working height. Kenyan buyers call it a chips fryer or a jua kali chips fryer machine, and it suits kibandas, fast food shops and canteens.

sections.heading: Key Features and Benefits
sections.body:
Two baskets in one tank. Fry two orders side by side, or keep one basket draining while the next batch cooks, so customers wait less.

Deep tank. A good depth of oil keeps the temperature steady when you drop in cold chips, which gives crisp, golden fries instead of soggy ones.

Strong mild steel stand. The welded square tube stand carries the full weight of the oil and holds the fryer at a safe height, away from children and traffic.

Easy to clean body. The smooth white and stainless body wipes down quickly at the end of a shift.

Locally fabricated. Made by our own fundis, so spare baskets and repairs are easy to get.

sections.heading: Who It Suits
sections.body: Chips kibandas, roadside fast food stalls, small hotels, school tuck shops and canteens that want a strong, affordable fryer that a local fundi can service. The tall stand also suits outdoor serving points and events where there is no counter to place a table top fryer.

sections.heading: What to Check Before Buying
sections.body: Check whether you will run it on gas or electricity, the floor space and ventilation. Tell us your busiest hour so we size the fryer correctly.

sections.heading: Care and Maintenance
sections.body: Strain the oil after each day, clean the tank and baskets, and wipe the outside. Check gas fittings or electrical cables regularly.

sections.heading: In Practice
sections.body: Fill the tank to the oil mark, heat it fully before the first batch and shake each basket half way through frying. Lift the basket, hook it on the edge to drain for a few seconds and serve. Keep a second basket loaded with cut chips so you never wait at peak hour.
